Two real issues: (1) the memo softens 'QPU not suitable for our work' to 'connectivity and size limits' - it was a forced fallback, not a deployment choice; (2) the future-advantage framing drops the paper's own admission that current QA already resembles classical thermal hopping. L3 #2 is the real one: memo says SQS 'converges toward classical baselines' but the asymmetry matters - XGBoost improves with more data while SVC degrades, and SQS tracks the SVC curve, not the class. That distinction is what defines the small-data niche for DT-QML-013. Fixes: (1) rewrite key_points[1] to flag the QSVM-vs-SVM claim as narrative/asserted, not benchmarked; (2) drop or qualify AT-QML-001 and AT-QML-005 attributions - paper provides no NISQ-ceiling or expressivity/trainability evidence; (3) add the historical-data limitation (regime-shift coverage bounded by historical sample); (4) tag the 40-60% number as framework-level (H3 on quantum is only partially supported per source).
